title: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: params, roles, stop/logprobs, streaming & structured output
author: Maya Thompson
description: This PR implements feature parity for the OpenAI /v1/chat.completions surface across Redwood's API layer and serving runtime. Motivation: customers expect drop-in compatibility for existing OpenAI chat workloads (params, role handling, stop sequences, logprobs, and response formatting) and stable streaming + function/tool call semantics. Changes cover: (1) request param mapping (temperature, top_p, n, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, max_tokens and client-sent stop sequences), (2) chat role normalization and system/user/assistant handling including legacy role aliases, (3) stop token handling applied both at tokenization and streaming time to ensure deterministic early termination, (4) logprobs support for allowed model backends with bounded memory usage, (5) streaming stability improvements to avoid truncated messages on network backpressure, (6) structured output compatibility (content filter for JSON blocks + schema-friendly formatting), and (7) OpenAI-compat response envelopes (usage fields, choices array, finish_reason mappings). The description below is an implementation summary and a short QA checklist. Implementation summary: - API layer: new openai_compat/chat_completions adapter that normalizes incoming body to internal request shape; preserves unknown params as pass-through. - Runtime: kernel-level early-stop hook and incremental logprobs emitter; streaming buffer flush on backpressure with sequence-framing to avoid corrupt partial JSON. - Tests: added unit tests for role permutations, stop sequences at chunk boundaries, logprobs size bounds, and full e2e with the openai-compat header. - Docs: updated docs/openai-compat.md with mapping table and migration notes. QA checklist: - [x] Param mapping matches OpenAI ordering and defaults - [x] stop sequences terminate both sync and streaming completions - [x] role aliases (assistant/system/user) preserved and canonicalized - [x] function/tool calls pass through and stream arguments reliably - [x] structured JSON output preserved across streaming reassembly - [x] CI integration tests pass against mocked model backends Notes and trade-offs: logprobs are enabled only for compatible quantized backends to avoid OOM; we emit a warning header when logprobs requested on incompatible runtime. Streaming changes add a small per-request buffer (configurable) to guarantee atomic choice emission. This is behind a feature flag (openai_compat_streaming_stability) until gradual rollout. Related: ENG-1245 (OpenAI parity epic), SUP-778 (customer report about truncated streaming).
